speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Example two is a lower-income family who recently admitted their severely disabled grandma to a nursing home.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The monthly out-of-pocket payment now is about $1,300.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In 2025, when the rebates kick in, this will decrease to $1,150.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In mid-2026, when the full enhancements are implemented, payments will further drop to about $1,000.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Example three is a disabled grandma from a lower-income family who has been staying in nursing homes for a few years now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The upcoming enhancements will formalise this temporary arrangement.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will continue working closely with providers to manage the fees that families have to pay, which should not change much this year.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Over time, their fees should rise gradually in tandem with inflation and income.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Chair, let me move to the second objective of public healthcare, which is to ensure availability.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Post-COVID-19, like many countries in the world, we saw many more seniors with complex conditions.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: A couple of years of isolation and neglect of chronic conditions have taken their toll.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The average length of stay in hospitals jumped abruptly from six days to seven days post-pandemic.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Sounds like one day, but it means a 15% increase in workload for hospitals.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have been doing major catch-up in infrastructure development.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Expanding capacity, however, does not mean just building hospitals.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We need smart capacity, across a spectrum of care needs and, especially, in the community.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Only then will we be able to give the most appropriate care for different types of patients.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This includes 1,200 acute hospital beds with the opening of Woodlands Health and across other hospitals.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We rolled out Mobile Inpatient Care@Home and commissioned 200 beds.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We opened new community hospitals and added 600 new beds and we also added 4,300 nursing home beds.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And adding nursing home beds is a major move, because if a senior cannot find a nursing home bed, they will end up in the hospital.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: With Woodlands Health, the capacity crunch at Khoo Teck Puat Hospital has finally eased after many years.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Bed occupancy has fallen from the typical 100% or more to now a healthier 85%.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Recently, the Singapore General Hospital opened an 80-bed acute medical ward to support its Emergency Department.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It caters to patients who have suffered, say, a fracture or you met with an accident and you are in shock.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, they are not in any danger, but they just need a short stay in hospital.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, this acute medical ward caters to this kind of patients and immediately provided relief to the Emergency Department.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: During COVID-19, Singapore General Hospital had to convert this link bridge between two blocks into bed space for Emergency Department patients that overspilled.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And no more space, we put them along the link bridge.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The beds were recently removed and the bridge is now open to pedestrians again and one of the final harrowing memories of COVID-19 has now been removed from SGH.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This includes about 2,800 public acute and community hospital beds to be added to Singapore General Hospital, Changi General Hospital, Sengkang General Hospital and also Woodlands Health.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will also add around 10,600 more nursing home beds.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But that is the number that we have to deal with as our population ages.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In the following decade from 2030 to 2040, the new Tengah General Hospital will open.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Singapore General Hospital campus and the National University Hospital Kent Ridge campus would have undergone major redevelopment to further improve national healthcare infrastructure.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The third and final objective is to ensure high quality.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This means that illnesses are effectively treated, patients’ preferences respected and innovative technologies leveraged to ensure patients can recover and get back to health quickly.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Kindness and care must fill our wards and clinics so patients do not feel alone in their journey of convalescence.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When a patient nears end-of-life, we walk the last mile with them and ensure that they leave peacefully.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What matters most to quality is actually our people.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Our healthcare workers, they are the driving force behind good care.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We saw that during COVID-19, and they deserve all our respect, appreciation and encouragement.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are not doing badly in retaining and attracting talent.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are fortunate that Singaporeans want to join the healthcare sector.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I always say, if you go to a primary school, for every 15 young students you see, one is likely to join healthcare.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For every 20 students you see, one is likely to become a nurse.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Regionally, we are an attractive place for foreign nurses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We worked with the Singapore Nursing Board to significantly reduce the processing time of registration applications from six months in the past to now, 30 days.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: With these moves, we become even more competitive.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In 2023, we recruited about 4,500 new nurses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Last year, we continued this momentum with another 3,800 new nurses and introduced the Award for Nurses' Grace, Excellence and Loyalty (ANGEL) scheme.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That was introduced in 2024 to encourage nurses to continue viewing their profession as an attractive long-term career.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Our healthcare workers, including junior doctors, they are dedicated and work very hard.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Heavy workload is a phenomenon in all developed countries, which are ageing and experiencing rising patient load.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Faisal Manap spoke up about the difficulties that junior doctors are facing.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: One, the Employment Act does not cover professionals, managers and executives (PMEs), including doctors.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The hours that you mentioned do not apply.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think many PMEs, including Members in this House, we work quite a number of hours, beyond what is specified in the Employment Act.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Number two, I hope Members do not go away thinking that we are facing a major outflow of doctors.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I wish it can be slightly lower, but actually, it is quite healthy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I want to emphasise: MOH has cared for our people and invested in them heavily for decades.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: From the moment they enter medical school, the subsidy we provide, the investment we made in our talent when they come into the system, going through housemanship, as a junior doctor, going through residency.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We invested heavily and we continue to invest heavily in our doctors.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But in championing the welfare of junior doctors, I urge Mr Faisal, too, to consider the interest of patients.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When pilots need to rest, passengers just have to wait for the next flight.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: All of us have experienced that in airports before.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If we do that for doctors, patients will be left untreated and their lives can be in danger.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, for MOH, we constantly have to balance the welfare of healthcare workers as well as patients.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If we suddenly limit the working hours of doctors, patients will suffer.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There have been many efforts for us to better manage these tensions, which the Senior Minister of State Dr Janil Puthucheary will elaborate on.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Transformation of our medical workforce is key to maintaining and improving quality of care.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The profiles of our patients are changing – generally older, with multiple health conditions requiring simultaneous management and coordination.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This means complementing specialists, who are very skilled in managing specific organ systems, with doctors with a broader breadth of expertise who can anchor, coordinate and manage cross-specialty issues for patients, which Dr Tan Wu Meng talked about.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This will enable us to deliver more holistic and integrated care, and it will be a key priority in the coming few years.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Besides the organisation of people, the ingenuity of our people matters just as much in driving quality.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In my view, these data should not be used to decide on issues, such as insurance underwriting, hiring people or granting of university places.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we will need broad public consultation for this legislation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Such a law is important to anchor the moral foundations of our society even as medical science breaks new grounds.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: With sufficient legal assurance, we will have the confidence to actively explore and experiment with the use of technology.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Singapore General Hospital is deploying an AI-powered app for parents to screen their babies for jaundice at home using their handphone with an app.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The app is trained with Singapore's multi-ethnic data and is sensitive to different skin tones.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: At the National University Hospital, doctors use AI to recommend treatment for patients by tapping into a vast database of historical caseload.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: With this tool, some doctors quipped that a junior doctor can now perform almost at the level of a senior doctor, because the experience is granted to them through AI.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In all these projects, the healthcare professionals remain in control of patient care and are enabled and enhanced by AI tools.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: By the end of this year, too, we hope all public health institutions will be able to use AI to automate and improve the accuracy of imaging scans, such as chest X-rays and mammograms.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng and Ms Ng Ling Ling asked about TCM.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The quality of our system can also improve if we can successfully integrate aspects of TCM proven to be safe and effective to complement Western medicine as part of mainstream healthcare.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Singapore is a multicultural country, open to learning from all parts of the world.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If there is a jurisdiction outside of Greater China that can blend and integrate Western medicine and TCM, it should be us.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We made a lot of progress in recent years.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We now have our own TCM degree delivered by the Nanyang Technological University enhanced professional training, we streamlined examination requirements and we are strengthening the TCM accreditation framework.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Today, certain acupuncture treatments are already incorporated in mainstream public hospital treatment.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Later this year, SingHealth and the Academy of Chinese Medicine, Singapore will be co-organising a forum on the integration of TCM and western medicine.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It will be attended by both TCM practitioners as well as Western doctors.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think it will be a great platform to explore further opportunities to identify further steps to synergise the strengths of both systems.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: (In Mandarin):   For seniors, a major concern is medical expenses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Most of them have retired and live on their savings.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When they need to use their savings to pay for medical expenses, they inevitably worry about not being able to afford them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Therefore, over the years, we have implemented many policies, including the Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation packages, as well as the Healthier SG and Age Well SG initiatives to reduce medical costs for our seniors.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Last year, we adjusted the CHAS eligibility criteria, allowing more CHAS Orange cardholders qualify for CHAS Blue cards.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: From time to time, Singaporeans ask MOH to provide more subsidies.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We understand this request and where reasonable and feasible, we will adopt these suggestions.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But as the saying goes, there is no such thing as a free lunch.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Whether it is more subsidies, more insurance payouts, or even free services, they all cost money.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And these costs are ultimately borne by citizens through fees, insurance premiums or taxes.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Through a multi-pronged approach of subsidies, insurance, MediSave and co-payment, we will continue to strive to reduce wastage of resources and avoid unnecessary treatment or overtreatment.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: By containing healthcare inflation, we can control the burden of cost for our people.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: For most people, the best way to ensure they can afford medical expenses is to maintain a healthy lifestyle and stay away from illnesses.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Many Singaporeans have actively participated, and more are starting to exercise more, which I find very encouraging.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Today, I hope to convince more seniors to stay physically and mentally active.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Besides doing exercise, seniors also need social circles to surround themselves with laughter.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: That is why we have established Active Ageing Centres across the country.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are providing these centres with more resources, to allow them to organise more activities and gatherings for seniors.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In my constituency, I am a loyal promoter of Active Ageing Centres and have gained some insights through this.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Inviting seniors to Active Ageing Centres is somewhat like making multiple visits to win someone over.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When seniors first hear about Active Ageing Centres, they may ask out of curiosity, "What are these centres?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Who built them?" Some might even ask volunteers, "Are you a property agent?" As we further explain the activities at Active Ageing Centres, seniors often become increasingly open to the idea of them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When we then tell them the centre has weekly communal meals and tell them, "Please come, it is on us", we then see the joy on their faces.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In ancient times, martial arts masters would fight and kill each other to obtain martial arts secrets.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But today, what we need are the secrets to good health, not martial arts.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These health secrets are in fact readily available – eat healthily, get sufficient sleep, exercise regularly, go for regular health screenings and visit Active Ageing Centres when you can.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: These are the secrets for good health. : Mr Chair, let me conclude.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I spoke about our plans to achieve our three big objectives of public healthcare.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: The problem is that they are competing objectives, a trilemma.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is impossible to achieve all three fully.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Indeed, in the UK, patients do not have to pay for public healthcare.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But as a result, demand shoots up and they now have seven million public patients on the waiting list for elective treatments.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked what can we learn from other countries, including the National Health Service?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think what we can learn from the National Health Service is to try not to be in the position they are in now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Switzerland adopts novel medical technologies and ranks top in the world for quality.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But about a quarter of the population chooses not to be treated, citing high cost.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Hence, high quality healthcare in Switzerland, but not so affordable.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If we are dogmatic and want to achieve one objective 100%, we pay a big price in the other objectives.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But if we take a more practical approach, we can balance the trade-offs and try to maybe achieve all three at 80%.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: A key to achieving these lies in a healthy population.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: With better health, we can achieve all three at the same time without trade-offs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Chairman, Dr Lim Wee Kiak talked about healthy longevity.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: A friend of mine, in his 70s and an avid golfer, once said that the perfect way for him to go is when he is 100 years old, playing golf, hits a beautiful shot, scores a hole-in-one, he is so happy, he collapses and dies.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: He may sound like he is joking, but I think he is dead serious.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: What he essentially described is the “holy grail” of healthcare where healthspan equals lifespan and you are healthy enough to do what you love until the last day.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This gap is quite consistent with most developed countries, but we must try to narrow it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Individually, too, we can all practise better preventive care and take better care of our own health.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Nationally, we need a major programme, hence Healthier SG.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Health screening, vaccination rates, they are all rising.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We are inculcating more good habits amongst our population.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And then, it will alert our Healthier SG doctor, who will, in turn, advise us what are the preventive steps to take.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is predictive preventive care – Healthier SG 2.0 – and we are not far away at all.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Mr Chairman, we are determined to expand healthcare capacity.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, even though we are rapidly ageing, healthcare must be available when Singaporeans need it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will develop our people, transform medical delivery and harness technology to continue to deliver high quality healthcare that Singaporeans deserve.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This Government understands that healthcare is a basic and essential public service that Singaporeans value.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have the experience, wherewithal, determination, ideas and policies to upkeep and strengthen this key tenet of our social compact.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Our agenda for healthcare is transformative and long term and will take us well beyond this Budget year.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I hope to have the continued strong support of this House, as we work together to overcome the mounting challenge of an ageing population, to cure sickness, to bring comfort to those in need and strengthen the health and happiness of all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, supporting the health and well-being of every Singaporean continues to be our approach to achieve a healthier nation and a more sustainable healthcare system.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our approach spans all life stages and today I will share our initiatives to support both the health of children and seniors.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Last year, we announced the completion of the Child and Maternal Health and Well-being Strategy and Action Plan that is applicable to children, adolescents and their families.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Neil Parekh asked about how Grow Well SG has been received thus far.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Many welcome this timely move to improve child health, especially MOH’s updated screen use guidance and refined practices on screen use management in preschools, primary and secondary schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We agree with Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Neil Parekh to reinforce families with practical resources and tools to support their children in building healthy habits, including good screen use habits, to improve their physical, mental and digital well-being.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: With work and family commitments, it can be difficult for parents to wean children off screens.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have, therefore, lined up tips and best practices to strengthen digital wellness efforts on various platforms, such as the Parent Hub websites, MOE Parents’ Gateway and MSF's Families for Life parenting programmes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Parenting for Wellness initiative is one example of the support available to families shared by MOE earlier.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We strongly encourage parents to adopt these strategies and actively foster healthy habits in their children.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will continue to work with preschools, schools, healthcare institutions and the community to educate and support families and children in reinforcing healthy habits.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Two initiatives announced earlier are the Health Plan and Childhood Health Behaviours Checklist.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Azizan, the son of Ms Nurhaslinda Wati, is one Primary 3 student who has benefited.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Health Plan motivated Azizan to continue his practice of healthy habits and taught him other interesting health tips.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: During the lifestyle discussion, Azizan was advised to continue his daily practice of choosing water as his preferred drink.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The lifestyle prescription played a pivotal role in encouraging Ms Nurhaslinda Wati to proactively work with Azizan to achieve his daily goal of choosing water over sugary drinks.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Their experience highlights how parents can engage their children to improve their health.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Dr Wan Rizal and Mr Neil Parekh also asked about our future plans for Grow Well SG.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Parents will be excited to know that the Health Plans will be expanded to Primary 4 and 5 students.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As the needs of upper primary students differ from those in lower primary, we will pilot this with some students this year to allow for calibration of the Health Plans and resources before full implementation in 2026.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Parents are encouraged to complete the checklist before or during visits.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This will allow them to discuss their child’s health behaviours on screen use, sleep, physical activity and nutrition with the healthcare professionals, and plan positive lifestyle changes at home.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Parents can also benefit from the resources on the recommended lifestyle behaviours via the weblinks and QR codes on each checklist.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The CHBC aims to encourage families to build healthy daily habits from young and will complement the personalised Health Plans children receive in primary schools.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We hope parents will tap on the Health Plans and CHBC to build and sustain healthy habits in children from birth through schooling years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: These small, consistent efforts can make a difference to your child’s health over time.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Apart from growing well, it is equally important to help our seniors age well in their communities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Assoc Prof Razwana Begum Abdul Rahim asked about the initiatives to promote healthy ageing.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: A key part of Age Well SG is our Active Ageing Centres.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: By the end of this month, we would have set up 223 centres, up from 154 when the scheme was announced.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We are devoting more resources to each centre, setting up more and working with the Ministry of National Development (MND) to locate them close to seniors’ homes.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This includes private estates which Ms Ng Ling Ling has asked about, so that they can better reach out to seniors and organise more and better activities.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond this, more seniors are volunteering as Silver Guardians at Active Ageing Centres.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Let us continue to make each Active Ageing Centre a vibrant hub for our seniors to gather with their friends, volunteer, keep active and stay healthy.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Our infrastructure has also been enhanced to make our flats, neighbourhoods and streets more senior-friendly, with various initiatives updated by MND and MOT.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We have completed our first Community Care Apartment, Harmony Village @ Bukit Batok, and are building more over the next few years.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: One resident at Harmony Village is Mdm Chia.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: After her husband passed away, she wanted to live in a place where she could retain her independence while receiving care support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This led her to choose the Community Care Apartment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Today, Mdm Chia is thriving at Harmony Village.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: She made many new friends, developed a close relationship with the Community Manager and actively participates in the activities, such as morning exercises, karaoke and communal lunches organised at the Community Care Apartment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling and Mr Yip Hon Weng asked about the plans for Shared Stay-in Senior Care Services Sandbox.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The service has been well-received by families, who play a key role in the caregiving journey by partnering providers in making caregiving decisions for their loved ones.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Seniors are also glad that they are able to age with peace of mind as their caregiving needs are taken care of around the clock.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The sandbox phase will be ended and we will continue supporting existing providers with work pass flexibilities while bringing new providers on board.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To better support providers, families and seniors, we will work with industry providers to formulate and publish a guide on the recommended good practices when providing or seeking such a service.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This service will not be licensed, as it provides caregiving support very much similar to how family members would care for their loved ones at home.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We welcome all providers to work with us on similar innovative care models to support ageing-in-place.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This complements existing options to provide care at home through video consults or home visits by healthcare providers, as raised by Dr Tan Wu Meng.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond innovative care models, we support the adoption of automation and technology solutions to increase productivity in the long-term care sector, as raised by Ms Ng Ling Ling.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: As pointed out by Mr Xie Yao Quan, it is also important to ensure the quality of our long-term care service.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is why we support providers to develop skilled manpower through a structured skills standards framework and subsidised training.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We agree with Dr Tan Wu Meng that care coordination is important to deliver good care.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This is why we are introducing the Integrated Community Care Provider (ICCP).

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: First, it is a dedicated point of contact for seniors and coordinates care among providers to provide long-term care services, such as active ageing and befriending, day care, rehabilitation and personal care support for activities of daily living.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Second, it allows seniors to receive a standardised care assessment for their long-term care needs.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Lastly, it develops one holistic long term care plan for more coordinated delivery across services.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: To implement this, we have divided Singapore into 85 sub-regions, with each sub-region having a dedicated ICCP appointed.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: For sub-regions with existing providers, we will facilitate partnerships.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: In other sub-regions, we have launched the process to select new ICCPs and will appoint them this year.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: This year, providers in several sub-regions will start providing joint programmes across their Active Ageing Centres.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Seniors with multiple care needs will also be seamlessly linked up across care partners in the same sub-region.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We agree with Mr Yip Hon Weng that a key concern our seniors have when it comes to ageing well is their ability to afford long-term care services when they need these.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The Prime Minister announced significant increases to long-term care subsidies and grants at the Budget to support seniors and their families, which Minister Ong has just explained.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Beyond these, we also have CareShield Life, our national long-term care insurance scheme that provides monthly cash payouts to policyholders who face severe disability.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: The scheme has not been reviewed since it was first launched in 2020.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Long-term care costs have since risen and we need to ensure that the payouts continue to provide meaningful support.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Therefore, the CareShield Life Council was asked to review the scheme.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: We will share more details in the second half of 2025 once the Council has completed its review.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Mr Chairman, in closing, we remain committed to provide the support needed for all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Second Minister for Health (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
text: Together, we can build a society where every Singaporean can grow, develop and age well, to enjoy a life of health and well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The role they play will only grow as the care needs of our ageing population become more complex.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They are critical to the Healthier SG initiative.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, family medicine is not listed as a recognised medical specialty in Singapore.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: With their broad skillsets and long-term relationships with patients, Family Medicine specialists will enable more patients with complex care needs to receive comprehensive care in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Further details on the entry criteria to become a Family Medicine specialist, training requirements and the implementation timeline will be shared later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: In advancing our primary care system, we will also ensure Singaporeans can access affordable care, including medications for chronic conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Today, the Healthier SG Chronic Tier offers enhanced subsidies for selected chronic medications at enrolled Healthier SG GP clinics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will continue to review the expansion of the range of medications which are subsidised under the Healthier SG Chronic Tier.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To respond to Dr Tan Wu Meng, today, polyclinics provide multiple appointment booking options, including online booking with staff guidance, phone bookings and walk-in services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Designated caregivers can also manage their dependant's appointment from their own HealthHub or cluster app account.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Urgent cases and patients who are frail or who have mobility issues will continue to be prioritised, even if they do not have a polyclinic appointment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Non-urgent cases may be scheduled for a later appointment or advised to seek treatment at a nearby CHAS GP clinic.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Subsidies for GP visits are also already available through CHAS, with enhanced benefits for Pioneer and Merdeka Generation seniors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Under Healthier SG, enrolled patients can access chronic medications at GP clinics at prices similar to polyclinics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MediSave can be used at both CHAS GP clinics and polyclinics.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Building on Minister Ong's earlier comments, let me elaborate our ongoing efforts to support our healthcare workforce.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Generations of doctors have indeed built our healthcare system through dedication and hard work under quite demanding schedules.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This applies to all of our professional colleagues – the allied health professionals; the nurses; the many, many staff members, who work together to make sure that our healthcare system functions for our patients.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We recognise that times and expectations have changed and our practices must evolve accordingly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, our public hospitals see many patients every day, with many requiring urgent, time-sensitive care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Shorter working hours mean more frequent handovers between doctors, requiring careful management and changes to work processes to prevent risks to patient care and longer waiting times.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have taken a measured approach to grow the healthcare workforce, including doctors, to meet the needs of our ageing population.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have already increased our annual intakes significantly.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: But we are mindful that, today, already one in 12 Singaporean students joins a healthcare programme and any significant expansion will require foreign healthcare professionals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We must take care not to deprive other important sectors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: And this raises a critical question: how do we balance our growing healthcare manpower needs against the many concerns raised in this House about foreign manpower dependency?

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As we grow the workforce, we have progressively made improvements, such as limiting junior doctors to 24 hours of continuous work periods and establishing rest day guidelines.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Nearly half of the clinical departments with junior doctors in public hospitals have adopted this and the rest will follow suit gradually.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I agree with Ms Mariam Jaafar, we must close the gaps in the treatment for physical health and mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This is why Healthier SG will include care for our residents' mental health.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These care protocols will ensure consistent and quality care are being delivered across primary care providers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We have also begun pairing Healthier SG clinics with Community Intervention Teams (COMIT) who provide psychosocial interventions for mental health needs in the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: They asked about costs, public awareness of programmes, like the Community Outreach Teams (CREST), and how effectiveness and progress in mental health programmes and care will be tracked.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Last year, during the Parliamentary Motion Debate on Advancing Mental Health, I shared our plan to have 90 CREST and 50 COMIT teams by 2030, including 15 youth-oriented teams each.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We are on track to achieve our targets.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: As one of the key first-stop touchpoints for in-person mental health services, CREST has strengthened local service linkages and networks across health and social care providers in the community, including GPs, polyclinics and hospitals.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To build greater awareness of CREST in the community, CREST teams conduct outreach to share information about their services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The Agency for Integrated Care (AIC) also promotes CREST through advertisements on social media, bus stops and HDB lift lobbies.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To further promote CREST, AIC has developed a Community Mental Health Wayfinding Tool, available on various platforms, including realspace.sg, mindline.sg and MindSG, to help users find the right mental health services, such as CREST.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The performance of CREST and COMIT teams, along with other public healthcare institutions (PHIs), such as our public hospitals and polyclinics, are assessed through key indicators such as access, response time, volume of clients supported, improvement in patients' outcomes and client satisfaction.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Patients' mental health outcomes are specifically measured through validated assessment tools, such as the World Health Organization (WHO) Disability Assessment Schedule and the Patient Health Questionnaire for depression, which assesses patients' functional levels and severity of symptoms.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The National Mental Health Office works closely with our PHIs and our community service providers to track and analyse aggregated data for the purposes of policy review, service planning and evaluating the effectiveness of our national mental health initiatives.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Eligible patients can also receive subsidised mental health treatment at polyclinics and participating GP clinics for the management of mental health conditions under the Chronic Disease Management Programme.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: At last year's debate, I also outlined our goal to train 130,000 frontline personnel and volunteers by 2030, to better equip them to identify individuals with signs of mental distress, provide a listening ear and refer them for support as needed.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I share Dr Wan Rizal's view that religious organisations must be part of our mental health ecosystem.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Since September 2024, the National Mental Health Office, together with AIC, has partnered with the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth to engage religious organisations and leaders, to provide them with mental health training programmes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The training equips participants with skillsets to provide basic emotional support, while ensuring that they understand when to refer individuals to professional mental health services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: When professional mental health care is required, religious leaders are encouraged to direct individuals to formal mental health services within the community.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: I agree with Mr Ong Hua Han that mental health first aid resources are crucial.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Meanwhile, we will continue to sustain our frontliner and volunteer training through structured mental health programmes, including e-learning modules developed by AIC and HPB, with psychological first aid training to be rolled out by mid-2025.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For members of the public, mindline.sg and MindSG offer comprehensive mental health resources, including information on supporting others and self-help tools.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mindline.sg also provides clinically validated self-assessment tools for depression and anxiety.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This round-the-clock service will feature an easy-to-remember four-digit number and offer chat support through the mindline.sg website.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This service streamlines access and connects Singaporeans to necessary resources.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: More details will be shared when the service launches later this year.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Wan Rizal asked about workplace mental health support.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Other initiatives include training employee peer supporters and conducting public education campaigns and workshops to combat workplace stigma, share best practices and facilitate employees' transition back to work.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Specialised employment support is available through agencies like Singapore Anglican Community Services, the Institute of Mental Health's Job Club and Singapore Association for Mental Health's MINDSET Learning Hub.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: These organisations offer customised vocational training and job placement services and have helped more than 6,000 individuals with mental health conditions gain and maintain employment.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We recognise the crucial role parents play in the minors' well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, the need for parental consent can sometimes deter minors from seeking help.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Parental involvement in their children's care journey is very important for better outcomes.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Co-developed by the National Council of Social Service and various stakeholders, including youths, "grovve" will be the first centre to provide integrated intervention services alongside general wellness activities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Its youth-centric location seeks to improve accessibility and normalise mental health care. "grovve" will foster communities where youths can become champions and supporters for mental well-being.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Mr Keith Chua asked about continuity of care, especially for those affected by suicide, and the coordinating role of the National Mental Health Office.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Suicide prevention and post-incident support requires a whole-of-Government and whole-of-society approach to address the issues holistically.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Existing community-based support available includes the Light in the Dark support programme by the Samaritans of Singapore (SOS) and the Live On! programme by TOUCH Community Services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Next-of-kin or loved ones affected by suicide may also benefit from suicide bereavement support programmes run by SOS, such as Healing Within and Healing Bridge, as well as Local Outreach to Suicide Survivors.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The National Mental Health Office coordinates with Ministries and agencies, including MOE, the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) and the Institute of Mental Health (IMH) in implementing policies and reviewing data and trends.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: A prime example of multi-stakeholder collaboration is the development of the Youth Crisis Facility.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It will support youths referred from the community or discharged from acute hospitals, offering psychosocial intervention in a safe and non-stigmatising environment to aid community re-integration.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The multi-stakeholder project team is currently developing clinical protocols and operational details for this facility, which will be a bridge between acute hospitals and community care.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng asked about insurers' practices for those with mental health history.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Apart from MediShield Life, which covers all Singapore Citizens and PRs, regardless of pre-existing conditions, including mental health conditions, individuals can opt for additional coverage through Integrated Shield Plans (IPs) and other private insurance plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: IP insurers' approach to underwriting persons with mental health conditions mirrors that of other conditions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: It is based on reliable information relevant to the risks being insured.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Factors considered may include age at the onset of condition, symptom severity, management of the condition and the presence of comorbidities.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: After the assessments, insurers may choose to accept applications as is, apply higher premiums, exclude specific benefits or reject applications in view of the risks presented, with proper justification to customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: There are cases where IP insurers have offered cover to customers with mental health conditions, either with or without exclusions.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: All IP insurers allow customers to request for a review of their exclusions or submit a fresh application if their condition has improved and they can provide favourable medical evidence.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: All insurers, including IP providers, are to adopt sound and objective processes to assess applications received from their customers.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: For example, insurers should not reject an application solely based on the customer's declaration of a mental health condition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Customers concerned about the underwriting decisions should raise the matter with their insurer for investigation or review.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: If they are not satisfied with the insurer's response, they can write to MOH or the Monetary Authority of Singapore to follow up and assess the full case details with consent.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: The increased focus on mental health in recent years has prompted changes in psychological practice, with more psychologists now working beyond traditional clinical settings in the community and private sector.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: An inter-agency implementation committee has been set up to look into this.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: This will raise professional standards, safeguard patient safety and increase public confidence in psychological services.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Further details will be announced at a later date.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: To prevent the public from being misled by services that are not licensed by MOH, the Healthcare Services Act (HCSA) currently prohibits providers of such services from advertising that they are able to "treat" a medical condition.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: However, certain professions, such as allied health and traditional Chinese medicine, are regulated under their respective professional Acts.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Even so, they will still have to ensure the accuracy of their advertisement.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Patients who now have to use different apps to access services at PHIs will be able to do so on this unified app in future for an improved, user-friendly experience.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will consider adding Healthy 365 to the unified platform in the future.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Ms He Ting Ru asked how we are harnessing the potential of precision medicine.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH is taking steps to embrace precision medicine in a cautious manner as we identify appropriate precision medicine applications with clear evidence of public benefit for scaling up.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We will also put in appropriate safeguards to mitigate risks, such as increased healthcare costs.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak asked about the potential of regenerative medicine.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: MOH has been supporting research in this through various schemes under the national Research, Innovation and Enterprise plans.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Health (Dr Janil Puthucheary)
text: We look forward to working closely with healthcare professionals, community partners and citizens to capitalise on these opportunities and effectively implement the initiatives I have covered today.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, my speech will cover the Ministry's efforts in three areas: firstly, on reshaping our norms and choices in healthy living; secondly, on maternity costs and fertility preservation; and lastly, on ensuring a robust healthcare workforce.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have made strides in our efforts to reduce sugar consumption.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As shared by Minister Ong, we will also tackle the issue of excessive intake of sodium and saturated fat.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ms Ng Ling Ling asked about the plans for extension of Nutri-Grade labelling for sodium and saturated fat in the F&B setting and the healthier alternatives that are available across cuisines.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We understand from engagements with the industry that tackling sodium and saturated fat content in eat-out dishes is challenging.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Given the diversity of cuisines in Singapore, the different cooking processes and recipes can lead to variations in the amount of sodium and saturated fat in a dish.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Instead, we are strengthening our engagements with F&B operators.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This includes ramping up voluntary store-front labels to help consumers identify stores that offer healthier dishes, either by using healthier ingredients or using less salt or sauces when cooking.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Besides encouraging F&B operators across various cuisines to use healthier ingredients and provide more healthier options through the Healthier Dining Programme, HPB is also actively engaging our hawkers on the importance of sodium reduction and providing them with samples of lower-sodium ingredients.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The availability and affordability of healthier ingredients for F&B operators and consumers are key to the success of our efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To this end, HPB's Healthier Ingredient Development Scheme supports manufacturers and suppliers in their reformulation efforts while reducing the price gap between healthier and regular versions.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue to build on these efforts to advocate for healthier meals that are lower in sodium, saturated fat and sugar.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Besides healthy eating, we must support active living.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to share the broader picture of healthy lifestyles and our progress towards shaping an active nation.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These activities are also now held at more than 1,300 locations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB has also expanded their programme offerings to cater to different segments.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: These include programmes, such as Steady Lah and Healthy Ageing Promotion Programme for You (HAPPY), to address frailty for seniors, Active Family Programme for young families, and Start2Move programme for individuals looking to kickstart an active lifestyle.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Everyone can now participate in activities suitable for their fitness level and at a convenient location.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We are heartened that the programmes have been well-received by Singaporeans.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To support Healthier SG GP clinics in encouraging appropriate physical activities for residents, HPB has also developed a guide to Lifestyle Prescriptions available on the AIC webpage.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The Healthier SG EventsGoWhere Portal was also launched last year to provide GPs and their care teams with a consolidated list of healthy lifestyle programmes from HPB, People's Association, SportSG and Active Ageing Centres to recommend to residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As we continue to build the infrastructure to encourage physical activity in the community, we have also been listening to residents' feedback.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We understand concerns over late arrivals and registration capacity for physical activity programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Some residents may also be unsure about the sign-up process.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For low and moderate intensity activities, including yoga, Zumba Gold and resistance band exercises, latecomers and walk-ins will be allowed, subject to capacity limits.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For safety reasons, higher-intensity activities like High Intensity Interval Training will still require punctual arrival, as proper warm-up and safety checks are needed to minimise injuries.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We encourage everyone to sign up for the activities via the Healthy 365 app and arrive on time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Prior to participating, residents should also monitor their own readiness and refrain from exercising if unwell.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With the changes, we hope more residents will join the variety of physical activity programmes conveniently located in their neighbourhoods.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We further recognise that some may prefer to exercise at their own pace and time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: HPB offers virtual physical activity sessions on Zoom and self-directed digital programmes.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: An example is the 12-week Age Strong programme which was launched in November 2024 on the Healthy 365 app, catering to residents aged 50 and above.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Participants can take part in customised workouts and learn about nutrient-rich diets and mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The programme also provides HealthPoints for completion of daily tasks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Users can set personalised activity goals for their physical daily activity and sleep duration to suit their preferences and daily routines and earn rewards for meeting their goals.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For those who have yet to come on board the Healthy 365 app, I urge you to be part of this journey to take steps towards better health.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: An area of growing concern that impacts on health and lifestyle is vaping.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng has expressed his concerns on this matter and urged stronger enforcement efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: MOH, in collaboration with various stakeholders, has intensified our whole-of-Government approach to combat vaping through public education and enforcement efforts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: As Mr Ang pointed out, there are some common misconceptions around vaping and, to this end, HPB has launched a series of campaigns over the last two years to increase awareness of the illegality and harms of vaping.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: To further amplify awareness, multiple channels, including social media and youth content creators, were engaged to more effectively reach the intended target audience.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Relevant stakeholders will continue to work closely to raise awareness among children and youths on the harms of vaping.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: On the enforcement front, the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) has increased enforcement operations, especially in public vaping hotspots, alongside other agencies, such as the National Environment Agency and National Parks Board.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Collaboration with the Immigration and Checkpoints Authority has also been strengthened to combat the smuggling of e-vaporisers at the borders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In educational institutions, the Ministry of Education maintains a firm stance against vaping, with disciplinary actions taken and referrals to HSA for offenders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Education and enforcement against vaping are a long-term effort, which will be continually monitored and reviewed to ensure we address the vaping issue effectively.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to say a few words in Malay. :   In our health promotion efforts, we should take an approach that is nuanced and suitable for the groups we are reaching out to.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This can only be done effectively if we work with a variety of groups and organisations in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For the Malay/Muslim community in Singapore, this is achieved through the Jaga Kesihatan, Jaga Ummah (JKJU) network, which comprises various organisations such as M³ agencies, Malay/Muslim bodies and religious organisations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This network, which initially started with just several mosques, has grown and continues to grow.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At the Sihat Bersama JKJU event last February, we acknowledged our partners and encouraged them to collaborate.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our partners also had the opportunity to showcase their efforts at the various booths which were also open to the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: At the Townhall session with me, Dr Wan Rizal and Ms Nadia Samdin, we openly discussed the health issues our community faces, how there is a socio-economic impact and different ways we can enhance our efforts to stay healthy holistically.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I am heartened by the discussions we had and our partners' commitment to making a difference as we move forward.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We have now entered the month of Ramadan and will continue with the programmes that have been planned.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This year, I am encouraged to see our JKJU partners expand and move towards a more holistic approach to health, while tailoring their activities to the needs of the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For instance, some of our M3 partners are collaborating with more JKJU Resource Partners like Caregivers Alliance Limited and the Stroke Services Improvement (SSI) Team under MOH to conduct talks on mental health and stroke awareness during this Ramadan, to promote heath screening and mental well-being.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Indeed, Ramadan provides a good opportunity for our community to make healthier choices a way of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: I urge the community to make the most of this time and bring about a positive shift in our lives. : For the next part of my speech, I will focus on family and fertility, which is an issue close to the hearts of many in this House.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Ms Sylvia Lim asked about the differences in maternity fees for Singapore Citizens and PRs as compared to non-residents.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: In fact, the vast majority of foreign mothers married to Singapore Citizens, and with Singapore Citizen children, are PRs or LTVP+ holders, and they would be eligible for these subsidies.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Expectant mothers married to Singapore Citizens may apply for an LTVP, and those who are eligible for an LTVP+ will be granted subsidies accordingly.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Beyond subsidies, the MediSave Maternity Package also allows couples to use their MediSave for their delivery and pre-delivery expenses.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Singapore Citizen or PR fathers whose spouses are giving birth in Singapore may tap on their MediSave to defray the out-of-pocket cost of their maternity fees.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For some individuals, however, the ability to build a family may be irreversibly compromised by medical treatments that are required to treat conditions, such as cancer.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Those who still face challenges with the cost of their fertility preservation treatments arising from medically necessary treatments may also approach medical social workers at their public healthcare institutions for further assistance, including to apply for MediFund.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: With these changes, we hope to assure patients facing medical challenges that their dreams of starting a family in the future are still within reach.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, allow me to move on to healthcare manpower.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: A strong healthcare workforce is vital to support both our preventive health initiatives and treatment needs, and we remain committed to building this capacity.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: The well-being of our healthcare workers, including nurses, continues to be a perennial concern.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: There are clear practices in our public healthcare institutions to ensure that nurses have sufficient rest during shifts.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: For example, nurses take staggered breaks during their shifts so that there is sufficient rest time for each nurse.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Dedicated rest areas, separate from clinical spaces, are also provided to ensure breaks are uninterrupted.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Between shifts, the clusters limit the number of consecutive working days.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Efforts have also been made to streamline processes and reduce administrative tasks so that nurses can complete their duties efficiently and end their shifts on time.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This decline in attrition, coupled with our sustained efforts to recruit new nurses, is helping to strengthen our nursing workforce and improve working conditions on the ground.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Ang Wei Neng asked about dental manpower sufficiency.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This is on par with other developed countries, such as South Korea and the UK.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Our local dentistry programme remains a steady and sufficient source of new dentists and hence, we do not currently provide pre-employment grants for dentistry.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: We will continue working with local Institutes of Higher Learning to meet national manpower needs for dental care.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Nonetheless, Dentistry students who choose to study overseas are welcome to return to Singapore to contribute as our healthcare needs expand.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: Mr Chairman, in closing, health is more than the absence of illness.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: It is about the quality of life for ourselves, our families and our communities.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: From nurturing healthy habits to family planning and ensuring the well-being of our healthcare professionals, we are building a system that supports Singaporeans at every stage of life.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Ms Rahayu Mahzam)
text: This journey requires our collective commitment and together, we can build a Singapore where every individual has improved opportunities and access to a more well-rounded, healthier life.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: Chairman, I just have one clarification for the Minister for Health.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: I am really glad to hear about increase in healthcare subsidies for Singaporeans because it is always a good thing, but if it is on the back of continually increasing cost, then it begs the question of sustainability and the tax burden on our future generations.

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: So, my question is: what are MOH's cost management strategies with the healthcare clusters?

speaker: Ms Ng Ling Ling
text: And how are efforts, such as what I read about NUH's value-based healthcare framework which measures value-driven outcomes, how is this initiative informing MOH on cost management?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: There is a range of things we do to manage healthcare cost.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We have a very disciplined system of what we call Health Technology Assessment (HTA), because there are so many new drugs today, so many new treatments.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Some treatments may be 10 times more expensive than current treatment but promised to cure another 2% to 5% more of the patient population.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Thirdly, as the Member mentioned, value-driven care actually is a major programme throughout our system.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If the Member is interested, she can file a PQ and I will see what data we can share.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But we are doing this across all institutions.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We measure the KPIs against cost and then have a sense of how much we are spending to deliver the KPIs and the objectives that we want to achieve.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Another major avenue to moderate cost is step-down care.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When capacity is misused, it leads to a lot of wastage and resources.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We used to have many what we call "social" stayers in our hospitals.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When I first joined MOH, we had something like 300 to 500 of them – basically, people who no longer needed to stay in hospital but they had nowhere else to go.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, we keep them in hospitals and sometimes, families even admit them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But today, with all the step-down care, we begin to be able to discharge them.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, from 300 down to 50, that is almost half a hospital freed up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We do benchmarking now across the system to make sure that there is price transparency and patients have a basis of comparison, what is a more cost-effective healthcare.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: If you notice this, we have started doing some enforcement on doctors that have overcharged and overclaimed MediShield Life and MediSave.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When you say healthcare is free at the point of care, actually it is not free.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Someone else still has to pay for it.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But to make it free for the patient means it is very expensive for the nation, because it will lead to a lot of excessive treatment and unnecessary servicing.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Actually, that is very good value for money.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, this is a summary of all the things that we are doing.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Healthcare costs cannot go on escalating like that.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I am hoping that this is a post-COVID-19 phenomenon, where healthcare costs escalated because manpower costs had jumped post-COVID-19.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Everyone, every country in the world realised that they need more manpower, they are hiring like mad and they have pushed up, globally, the cost of healthcare manpower.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But I hope, at some point, this will stabilise.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: You will start to track general inflation rather than leads general inflation.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: I welcome the increase in the MediSave outpatient withdrawal limits.

speaker: Ms Hazel Poa
text: These amounts, I believe, were also set in 2021.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
