text: Chair, before I answer Ms Hazel Poa's question, I forgot that I need to clarify two factual errors in my speech.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: First, when I was mentioning the attrition rate of junior doctors, I mentioned 7%.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When I was showing a chart, I mentioned that for long-term care, for those who were born in 1969 or earlier, they have an additional subsidy.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I said the reason is because they are less covered by MediShield Life.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is that they are less covered by CareShield Life.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I know where she is coming from, because the Basic Retirement Sum and Basic Healthcare Sum are rising in tandem with inflation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Which is correct, because these are amounts of money that you want to save up for your old age and, therefore, when you spend, you must make sure what you set aside grows in tandem with inflation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: However, when it comes to the claim limits of Flexi-MediSave or MediShield $500/$700, these are more policy-driven.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Take, for example, today, we just announce that you can use MediSave to co-pay for dental root canal.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Sometime ago, we say, we are subsidising Shingles vaccination and, whatever is the co-payment, you can use MediSave.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Once we allow that, suddenly the demand for MediSave spending goes up.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Over five years, it has doubled from $200 to $400.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, if you have tracked inflation, actually, the increase will be much less.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But because this is a lot more driven by policy, we adjust them instead every few years, taking into account general inflation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think that is a much more practical approach.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: First one is for the Minister on TCM.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: So, beyond acupunctures, how is TCM also being integrated with the mainstream healthcare system?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Are there plans to develop specialist roles for TCM practitioners?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: And are there plans for the Civil Service to eventually recognise the MC issued by the TCM practitioners?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: The second clarification is for Minister of State Rahayu on vaping.

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: Did HSA discover any platform in Singapore that sell vapourisers or the operators in Singapore?

speaker: Mr Ang Wei Neng
text: If so, will HSA consider prosecuting the platforms to have a deterrence effect?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, the quality and the delivery of services has a big variation.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think we ought to be quite careful and always take an evidence-based approach.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Take certain treatments that we think has potential, has worked well in other countries, with evidence in existing literature, try it in our system, and if it works, we can then bring it into the mainstream.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, we are doing use case by use case, using an evidence-based approach.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Because it is a self-regulated system, it will be difficult for Civil Service or otherwise to pass a law to say that TCM MCs will be recognised.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: In any case, I think good human resource practice is to be able to tell your employees that when you are ill, call in sick.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: You do not have to produce an medical certificate and make an additional trip, either to TCM or to the polyclinic just to get the medical certificate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Actually, the Civil Service has already moved towards that.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think there are a few days in the year that you actually do not have to produce an medical certificate.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: You can call in sick and I think that is a better HR practice.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: Indeed, HSA does monitor regularly on the upstream sales that we see on the online spaces and HSA actually works closely with the platforms to ask them to take down all the postings on the illegal sales of such product.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, HSA collaborates with platforms, like Instagram, Carousell and Facebook, to remove the postings.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: And MOH and HSA are currently working with MDDI as well to see how we can encourage social media platforms to further strengthen this effort to detect and remove these online sales of advertisements on e-vapourisers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: This is something that I understand is a worrying concern and we will continue to look at how we can enhance our efforts in this space.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I have a clarification for Minister of State Rahayu about the cut on maternity fees which I filed.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: I filed this actually based on some ground feedback that came to me from my residents who are Singaporean fathers-to-be but their wives are foreigners.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: They may be holding LTVP, not plus, or something lesser.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: And from our research on the KK Women's and Children's Hospital website, it does appear that the maternity fees that are charged are actually tied to the residency status of the mother.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, I do not know whether earlier, because I did not hear her that carefully, was the Minister of State Rahayu saying that somehow the father's status as a Singaporean can be taken into account to reduce the maternity fees in such situations?

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Because I did not hear that very clearly and I would like her to clarify that.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So, actually, what I said was that foreign mothers who are married to Singapore Citizen fathers and, who are PRs or on LTVP+, can receive Singapore Citizen-level subsidies for delivery episode, in recognition that their child will be a Singapore Citizen; and PR-level healthcare subsidies for all in-patient services.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: So forth, for maternity care, when it is the delivery, they will actually get Singapore Citizen-level subsidies.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua
text: In a PQ I filed last year, the response advised that there is no tracking or cumulative data collated of the number of persons diagnosed with suicidal ideation, whether caused by mental health conditions or other triggers.

speaker: Mr Keith Chua
text: Will MOH reconsider the current position, now that we have the National Mental Health Office, as this monitoring or tracking should be helpful in suicide prevention and, perhaps, more importantly, the provision of resources required for the support of these individuals?

speaker: Mr Keith Chua
text: We should do all within our means to prevent the next suicide.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But I do not want to overstate it, that this particular data variable that Mr Chua has identified is already in the works.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I will have to go and have a look at the kind of data that we can provide on a robust basis year-on-year.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: And part of the issue, of course, is that the providers that we have within the space are very varied, and this is not necessarily something that is always reported.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, we have got to look to see how we can make sure that we have this data in a robust manner, so that the number that we are reporting and tracking is something that informs what we do with our policy as well as our operations.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Does the Minister recognise that Singaporeans are not visiting their dentist frequently enough for regular checkups?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: As I mentioned in my cut, while over 50% visit a dentist at least once a year, 40% of these visits are for reactive treatment rather than for preventive care.

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: Are there plans to encourage more frequent visits to the dentist of at least 12 to 18 months?

speaker: Mr Gerald Giam Yean Song
text: And does MOH have plans to expand the capacity of public dental services to meet this increased demand?

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I would say, the polyclinics are quite busy, but we can leverage private clinics more for preventive oral care.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: My hypothesis is that when you go to a private clinic because you have a decayed tooth, the dentist says you need a root canal.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It requires quite a few trips to the clinic, and so, you would rather extract or, in the first place, let us not go to the dentists.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: With this step and with some more education, including a national dental plan that we are now drawing up, we hope that more people are aware of the importance of oral health and understand that any restorative treatment, and for orange CHAS cardholder's preventive care treatment, they will all be better subsidised now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I think more people will come forward and we can better leverage and better use the capacity we have today in all the private dental clinics.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: So, I think this is an important step we are first taking and we are still reviewing and drawing up our national dental plan.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And can I ask MOH if, moving forward, there will be even greater attention given to how we measure value, not just in terms of a single Ministry policy at one point in time, but also looking at how it may shape the situation for the family.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, for example, if additional manpower and resources are needed so that a particular patient does not have to attend 36 appointments a year, but let us say, down to 18 or 12, those resources in streamlining and coordinating care can be looked in context of reducing the effort needed by the caregiver who accompanies the patient.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Because, as I have said during the Budget debate, this can determine whether the caregiver goes from full-time to part-time employment, or whether a caregiver on flexible work leaves their career completely.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And, therefore, the support to the patient can also be considered in terms of the outcomes for the family unit and the family unit's ability to continue being in employment.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I can appreciate where the Member is coming from.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: When you have so many appointments, the toll on the caregiver is quite immense and it all looks a bit inefficient.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But the Member also works in a hospital, there are so many specialties and sub-specialties, and when someone is senior, they start to have many different problems with many different organs.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And therefore, while we can coordinate, they still require review by several specialists.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: We will try to streamline as much as we can, but I do not think there can be a major streamlining and cutting down of appointments.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Having said that, as I mentioned to Ms Ng Ling Ling, there are a range of things we are doing to moderate healthcare costs, and if we can do so and keep people healthy, we also will be able to reduce the burden of caregivers.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: I would say we are going far beyond measuring value now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: Value-driven care (VDC), as I was telling one consultant, is old technology for health system.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: And today, I think health economists do recognise that with VDC, you can eliminate operational or clinical or disease level wastage.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: But with the ageing population we need to eliminate population level wastage.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It means it is no longer just about how you treat this person in the most efficient way and cost effective way possible.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is about saying that this person should not be here in the first place.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: This is the level of efficiency that we are going to achieve now.

speaker: Mr Ong Ye Kung
text: It is many years of transformation ahead and we will work together.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: A clarification for the Senior Minister of State.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I think Senior Minister of State mentioned earlier that they are working towards registration for a subset of psychologists, if I understood him correctly.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: So, I just wanted to check with the Senior Minister of State whether there are plans, as I mentioned in my cut, to also include other mental health professionals, such as psychotherapists and counsellors, just because these are also professionals who work with vulnerable clients.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I believe that, anecdotally, some practitioners have also shared with me their concerns that there are people out there holding themselves out to be therapists after doing some online courses or a weekend class in an area.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: I think this causes a little bit of concern because, after all, the clients who come to them for help are usually pretty vulnerable individuals.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And relatedly, I was also wondering what sort of public or consumer education is being undertaken so that members of the public who are seeking help can understand, for example, what is the difference between a psychotherapist, a counsellor, a psychologist, a psychiatrist.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: A lot of my residents who come to me, struggle to understand the difference and know where is the best place to seek help.

speaker: Ms He Ting Ru (Sengkang)
text: And also, if they have some concerns about the person they are actually seeking services from, where do they go if they have got a complaint or they have got some concerns about some of the sessions that they are having with them.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We are early in the process, so some of these details have not yet been established.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: But let me try to perhaps explain how we are thinking about this.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: We do indeed want to protect vulnerable individuals, and she has highlighted how someone who is seeking these sorts of services may well be in a position where they are vulnerable if not dealt with properly or dealt with by someone who is not entirely professional.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, that is the perspective we are coming from.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: How do we protect individuals seeking these services and at the same time raise the standards and quality of the profession?

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The resources then for further information actually are already available.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: I mentioned quite a few of them in my speech.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: The websites, the chatlines,and then later on this year we will have the hotline.

speaker: Dr Janil Puthucheary
text: So, a member of the public who is concerned about the therapies that they are getting can access any one of these resources or contact MOH directly and we can also provide advice.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I think all the clarifications have — Well, I spoke too soon.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: Earlier she, she mentioned that citizen level subsidies would be available for delivery by foreign mothers if they are PRs or LTVP+ holders, in consideration of the fact that the child will be a Singapore Citizen.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: But I think she will also know that there are Singapore children also being born to mothers who are LTVP, but not plus.

speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
text: So, can that not also be considered in the fee setting?

speaker: The Chairman
text: And with that I believe all the clarifications have been answered.

speaker: The Chairman
text: I am very glad that this is the first Head where we have finished ahead of the guillotine time.

speaker: The Chairman
text: Having said that, Dr Tan, would you like to draw your amendment?

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Mr Chairman, I thank all who contributed to this debate.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Our MOH leadership and MPs of all persuasions.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Also want to express deepest thanks to our entire healthcare family, our front liners, the support team and our public officers.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: If I may briefly seek the indulgence of Speaker —

speaker: The Chairman
text: Dr Tan, I was not asking you to make a long closing, please.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: So, if I may just recall briefly what I said five years ago during the debate on the President's Address.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: Healthcare is about all our people's lives, your life and mine, the lives of our loved ones, the life of every Singaporean.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: And with that, let us all hope for healthier and happier lives together.
